## Verdict

missing

## Bearer

ProfileSyncListenerService — app-wear/src/main/java/com/mgilli/app_wear/sync/ProfileSyncListenerService.kt

## Trigger

Receiving a profile-sync message on the Wearable Data Layer, in
`onMessageReceived` — observed

## Today

`onMessageReceived` decodes the incoming payload, then on decode
success calls `profileSyncPushService.applyIncoming(payload,
clock.now())` at line 53 and discards its returned
`ProfileSyncApplyOutcome` entirely: neither `Refused` nor `Failure` is
read or logged. `RecordedRaceListenerService` and
`RecordedRaceAckListenerService`, the module's other two listener
services, both log their failure outcomes at ERROR — a decoding
failure and an `acknowledge` failure respectively — so the repository
already carries the correct form for this defect, in the same folder.

A second, independent instance of the same defect exists on
`WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService.kt:47`:
`raceRecordingRepository.findInProgress().getOrNull()` reads the
result of a store call and discards its failure branch, so a store
failure renders identically to "no race in progress" and the
complication silently clears from the watch face with nothing said
about why. This is the same call site D15 already names for
`WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService`'s reliance on
`WatchRaceNavigator`, and D5 already names the analogous `getOrNull()`
drop in `WatchApp`.

## Expected

`onMessageReceived` reads the `ProfileSyncApplyOutcome` returned by
`applyIncoming` and logs `Refused` and `Failure` at ERROR, naming the
operation and the outcome, the same way `RecordedRaceAckListenerService`
logs `acknowledge`'s failure today.

A second gap, on the same pattern but a different bearer:
`WatchRaceComplicationDataSourceService.onComplicationRequest` calls
`raceRecordingRepository.findInProgress()` and discards its `Result`'s
failure branch through `getOrNull()`. It must instead read that
`Result`, log a store failure at ERROR distinctly from the nominal
"no race in progress" case, and — per D15's note that this same entry
point must render an empty complication rather than let an exception
escape — still hand the complication data source an empty result on
that failure rather than leaving the request unanswered.

Neither log message may carry race data, a heart-rate reading, a zone,
a duration, a pace, a race name or a race date (R54); each names only
the operation and the failure.
